text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved pegging the lev to the German mark as anchor currency in a currency board system at an exchange rate of 1,000 per mark.
-- Bulgaria expects to sell 4,000 state plants by the end of next year, deputy prime minister Alexander Bozhkov told a business seminar in Sofia. @

-- France is expected next week to extradite to Bulgaria Ivo Nedialkov, under investigaton in Bulgaria for misappropriating some $6 million in 1994 through a get-rich-quick scheme, the National Investigation Service said.
-- Bulgaria's National Social Insurance Institute said it would discuss today a possible rise of the minimum pension to 27,000 levs from 16,300 levs from July.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said it had sealed a contract for the sale of a 70 percent of the Interpred World Trade Centre in Sofia to South Korean Daewoo Corp for $20 million.

-- Bulgaria's police said it had found the perpetrators of a bank robbery who siphoned 180 million levs from Bulgaria's state Post Bank head office in Sofia through a documentary fraud on Friday. Some 78 million levs have been already restored to the bank.

-- Bulgaria's deputy Alexander Karakachanov, elected on the ticket of the Union for National Salvation, said he had submited to parliament a draft bill to overrule bank secrecy regulations for cases of overdue credits over 500,000 levs.
-- The staff of Bulgaria's state cannery Ketchup Fruct bought 60 percent stake in the company for 520 million levs, state BTA agency said.
-- Bulgaria can not give up nuclear power production but the country will not build a second nuclear power plant, Prime minister Ivan Kostov said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
